summary: Iter 153 chat-streaming (SSE) end-to-end verified. Backend: 7/7 pytest passed (existing test_iter153_chat_stream.py 3/3 + 4 new edge cases: 422 validation, 401 on history, no Mongo _id, cross-user session isolation). Frontend (accelerator@wladbot.test): short message streamed into [chat-ai-message-streaming] with caret after ~1.5s, 'Wlad denkt nach' vanished on first token, finalized as [chat-ai-message] with 'Kopieren' + 2 follow-up chips, no leftover draft/caret, 0 console errors, session appears in 'Deine Chats'. Long deep-model message (267 chars): first tokens 1.8s, monotonic growth 134->2671 chars, done at 50s, 2 chips. Follow-up chip click auto-sends a new user message and streams the reply (4.3s). Reload -> latest session auto-loads persisted streamed answer (2904 chars) + chips + copy button. Coach mode: uses classic POST /chat (network log shows /chat only), thinking indicator shown, NO streaming bubble, structured card (Strategie / numbered steps / reflection / task suggestion) renders. 'Aufgaben aus dem Gespraech erstellen' works and returns a task suggestion card. Usage-feedback popup measured at x=1440,y=927 — no geometric overlap with chat input (x694-1326) or send button. Free user (free@wladbot.test, balance 26) streamed one message successfully, no broken draft bubble. Total ~7 LLM calls used.
critical_code_review_comments: Non-blocking: [data-testid=chat-input] is NOT disabled during loading/streaming (only the send button is). Double-send is prevented by the `if (!text || loading) return;` guard in handleSend, so this is safe — but the spec claim 'input remains disabled while loading' is not literally implemented; consider disabling or keep as-is intentionally (typing ahead is arguably better UX).

Non-blocking: streamChat() is called without an AbortSignal in ChatPage.handleSend — navigating away or unmounting mid-stream leaves the fetch/reader running and setMessages may fire on an unmounted tree. Passing an AbortController tied to a cleanup effect would be cleaner.

Observation (transient, not reproducible in the 2nd run): in one run the visible length of the streaming bubble momentarily shrank (337 -> 17 chars) before growing to the full 782-char answer. Most likely SmartText re-parsing an incomplete markdown list mid-stream; second run showed strictly monotonic growth (134/476/761/1164/1479/1854/2219/2671). Worth a quick look at SmartText's handling of partially-received markdown, low priority.

402 paywall path for /chat/stream is structurally correct (credit check happens in _prepare_chat BEFORE StreamingResponse, so the client gets a real HTTP 402 that ChatPage maps to the paywall modal) — could not be exercised live because free@wladbot.test still had 26 credits and burning them was out of scope.
